title: SiteLens
description: UX design and research for SiteLens, AR-glasses overlays and a companion mobile app for construction inspectors, designed over five weeks.
hmw: empower inspectors and project managers to streamline on-site construction inspections by overlaying dynamic checklists, contextual data, and real-time collaboration tools through AR glasses, while reducing costs and ensuring compliance?

heroImages.alt: two people in yellow jackets sitting on steps
man in yellow shirt and black pants standing on gray concrete floor

blocks.text: Inspectors need role-specific checklists, before/after comparisons and cost verification while they work on site. Over five weeks, I was the UX designer and researcher on SiteLens: AR-glasses overlays and a companion mobile app for them.

items: Streamline inspection flows
Improve data and accuracy
Reduce costs and increase efficiency
Enhance collaboration and compliance
Future-proof AI + AR

items.title: Research & Discovery

items: Conducted competitive audits of existing construction inspection apps and AR-enabled field tools.
Interviewed inspectors, project managers, and engineers across trades to uncover pain points in workflows, checklists, and reporting.
Identified high-need use cases: role-specific inspection checklists, before/after comparisons, and cost verification workflows.

items.condensed: I audited inspection tools and interviewed inspectors, managers and engineers, which surfaced role-specific checklists, before/after comparisons and cost verification.

items.title: Literature Review

items: Reviewed academic and industry sources on AR in construction, wearable-assisted inspections, and spatial computing.
Explored challenges in data compliance, law/recall notifications and construction order finalization.
Identified trust, accuracy, and real-time collaboration as essential UX considerations, beyond hardware specs.
Used findings to inform principles for checklist design, visual layering, and mobile–AR integration.

items.condensed: I reviewed research on construction AR and wearables, focusing on data compliance, legal notifications, and real-time collaboration requirements.

items.title: Stakeholder Interviews

source.text: Interviewed stakeholders to capture tool requirements.

items: Used insights to shape inspection templates, room-based checklists and tailored dashboards.
Captured requirements for role-specific tool lists (e.g., scanner, notes, tape measure).
Helped refine the goals of cost reduction, accuracy and real-time updates across multiple contractors.

items.condensed: I interviewed field stakeholders to capture tool requirements and design room-based inspection checklists, tailored dashboards, and contractor workflows.

items.title: Usability Evaluations

source.text: Tested prototypes with users to assess readability, voice and gesture commands, and efficiency.

items: Gathered feedback on AR checklist readability, voice/gesture commands and navigation triggers.
Measured efficiency: time saved compared with manual inspections and paper-based workflows.
Used findings to refine visual hierarchy, session summaries and integration with maps and reminders.

items.condensed: I tested AR prototypes with field users to measure time saved over paper workflows and improve voice commands and readability.

items.title: Design & Prototyping

items: Developed low- and high-fidelity prototypes for mobile and AR glasses.
Designed a modular UI system for uploading inspection checklists, attaching before/after photos, and role-based task lists.
Prototyped AR overlays including: room-wise task lists, video-assisted inspection references, law/recall notifications, and cost/order verification prompts.
Created interactive flows simulating site inspections with Even Realities G1 glasses.
Iterated prototypes with stakeholders for validation and alignment with real-world workflows.

items.condensed: I built prototypes for mobile and Even Realities G1 glasses, testing room-wise task overlays, photo attachments, and verification prompts.

items: Dashboard Banner: Displays AR-driven task information (to-do list, floor plan, live inspection data).
AI Status Module (Omni-AI, Excellent): Real-time system feedback on inspection/AI status.
Active Apps Section: Toggle control for apps in use (To-Do List, Map).
Inactive Apps Section: Secondary options (Translate, Camera) to activate as needed.
Suggested Apps: Personalized extension discovery with one-tap install (App Store style).
Top Navigation: User/account access via profile + notifications.

cards.label: Productivity First
cards.value: Prioritizes utility and tools, not just media.

cards.label: Modular + Flexible
cards.value: Clear segmentation between active, inactive, and suggested apps makes system extensible.

cards.label: Mobile–AR Bridge:
cards.value: Designed to mirror AR glasses UI (simple toggles, spatial task context).

cards.label: Trust-building
cards.value: Omni-AI status builds confidence by surfacing clarity (“Excellent”) upfront.

items: Content-centric: Prioritizes large thumbnails so users can browse visually, reducing cognitive load.
Simplicity + Familiarity: Mirrors social apps (Instagram Explore, YouTube library), making it intuitive.
Scalable: Grid layout supports expansion to more media types (photos, 360 images, AR models).
Contribution-first: The purple upload CTA signals active participation, not just passive browsing.

cards.label: Upload Media Button
cards.value: Prominent call-to-action in the center, encouraging contribution.

cards.label: Popular Content Grid
cards.value: Visual-first layout with thumbnails, titles, and quick delete (X) actions.

blocks.text: Three calls that shaped the home screen

cards.label: Productivity first
cards.value: Chose a home built around utility and tools over a media-first one.

cards.label: Active, inactive, suggested
cards.value: Chose clear segments for active, inactive and suggested apps, because they keep the system extensible.

cards.label: Mirror the glasses
cards.value: Chose a mobile UI that mirrors the AR glasses (simple toggles, spatial task context), so the two feel like one system, with an Omni-AI status that builds confidence by showing clarity upfront.

items: The usability sessions measured time saved against paper workflows, but this study states no figure, so I make no efficiency claim.
The glasses flows were interactive prototypes simulating site inspections on Even Realities G1 glasses, not a deployed tool.
